newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK governor reminds Tung he is in charge until '97.
newsitem.headline: HK governor reminds Tung he is in charge until '97.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten reminded Hong Kong's leader-in-waiting on Wednesday that he was in charge until the stroke of midnight next June 30 but was willing to lend a hand to ensure a smooth handover to China.

"We are both, of course, agreed that I am responsible for the administration of Hong Kong until June 30 next year and after that he (Tung Chee-hwa) is responsible," Patten told reporters after a university commencement ceremony.
"And I will not during the course of the next months seek to interfere in any way in matters which are properly his responsibility as the chief executive after July 1 next year."
A 400-member Selection Committee assembled by China overwhelmingly voted in Tung as chief executive-designate on Wednesday.
Patten said Tung would face challenges and difficulties as the leader of Hong Kong but added he would have "the good wishes of the community".
"But I am sure he will do the job well, standing up for Hong Kong's autonomy, which is of course essential," Patten said.

"I am sure the whole community will also hope that he will stand up for Hong Kong's rule of law and stand up as well for all those things which have made Hong Kong so successful over the last few years."

Earlier in the day, Patten congratulated the shipping tycoon -- a former member of his Executive Council -- and pledged "all necessary assistance" from the government in Tung's preparations to assume office in less than seven months.
"I wish Mr Tung every success in his endeavour and I have congratulated him personally," Patten said in a statement.
Tung resigned from Patten's inner cabinet of advisers to vie for the post of chief executive.
He will take the helm when Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, is returned to China at midnight on June 30 next year under the terms of a 1984 Sino-British treaty.

Beijing has declared that Hong Kong will become a Special Administrative Region, permitted considerable autonomy and allowed to maintain its capitalist way of life for 50 years under paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's one country, two systems policy.
